task_text: Fix split_fields(text) in solution.py. Unescaped commas split fields; backslash escapes ONLY comma or backslash; preserve empty fields including trailing ones. Empty input returns ['']. Invalid escape or dangling backslash raises ValueError. No imports or external dependencies. Return full solution.py in files, with only pure functions; allowed built-ins len/range/enumerate/zip/sorted/list/tuple/str/int/float/bool/abs/min/max/sum/round/ValueError; the only allowed method call is list.append. Do not include grading tests. answer may briefly identify the implementation. Host checks run separately. Inputs are strings, at most80 characters.

answer.implementation: single-pass index scan; walks text char by char, escapes only comma/backslash after a backslash, appends completed field to a list on each unescaped comma, raises ValueError on dangling or invalid backslash escapes

response.concise_method_summary: Replaced naive text.split(",") with a manual single-pass scan over the string using an index i and accumulator string current. On each character: if it's a backslash, check bounds (raise ValueError if dangling at end of string), then check the next character; if it's ',' or '\\' append that literal character to current and advance i by 2, otherwise raise ValueError for invalid escape. If the character is an unescaped ',', append current to the fields list and reset current, advancing i by 1. Otherwise append the character to current and advance i by 1. After the loop, append the final current to fields (handles empty input and trailing empty fields correctly, since fields always ends with one append per field regardless of comma count). Only list.append is used as a method call; only len, range-free indexing/while loop, and ValueError are used from the allowed set; no imports.
assumptions: Escaped characters other than ',' and '\\' following a backslash are invalid and must raise ValueError
A backslash as the last character of the string (nothing to escape) is a dangling backslash and must raise ValueError
Fields are joined by commas only at the top level; no nested quoting/other delimiters are relevant
Input is always a str up to 80 characters as stated; no non-string input handling needed
proposed_verification: split_fields('a\\') raises ValueError (dangling backslash) and split_fields('a\\n') raises ValueError (invalid escape)
